object_description: compact square composition organized around an atrium
design_condition: The building is set back from the street and community center, leaving a diffuse relationship between the public road, village square, outside space, and parking; the cramped gaps and temporary expansion position weaken the overall site-planning concept.

positive.statement: The expansion of the common room into the playground is very inspiring.
The central two-story room with its grandstand-like staircase and slide creates an inspiring access and communication space.
The connected common room and terrace create a distinct atmosphere.
The project offers substantial spatial potential for an open house and a unique organizational culture.
The project impresses with its compactness.
The hybrid construction method is conceptually comprehensible and coherently presented.
The project is within a good cost range and aims at sustainability in a holistic sense.

negative.statement: The positioning of the building body is not convincing from a site-planning perspective.
Direct visibility from the sidewalk into the kindergarten rooms makes the transition impractical.
The space between the secondary school and playgroup is too cramped.
The area in front of the building and the public-road relationship remain diffuse and lack sufficient significance.
The open spatial organization causes mutual interference that must be taken into account.
The spatial closure of the common room and access to a playgroup room are not functionally solved, calling the claimed flexibility into question.
The second garden exit is schematic and leaves too little space for kindergarten cloakrooms.
The large upper terrace has not been shown to achieve a quality comparable to the central interior.
Fire protection and the fully glazed sloping roof areas present complex structural and energy-related challenges.
The architecture refers too much to itself and does not establish enough connection with the public space and surrounding architecture.
